title: Magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density of inhomogeneous superconducting films: the Tc-mosaic model
abstract: Whole-sample and mutual-inductance part-sample measurements of the linear magnetic susceptibility, $χ$, of superconducting films are routinely used to obtain the London penetration depth, $λ(T)$, assuming uniform superconductivity. However, spatially resolved probes show that many films of current interest are inhomogeneous on micrometer scales. Here we ask whether a distribution of local transition temperatures in a fully gapped film can produce an apparent line-nodal, $T$-linear $λ(T)$. The film is modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains with $T_c$ distributed between $T_{c,\min}$ and $T_{c,\max}$ with s-wave (also d-wave, for comparison) London response inside each domain. We show that detectable screening appears only below the percolation temperature, $T_p$, and the transition broadens with the spread of $T_c$. For s-wave domains, $λ(T)$ remains activated for any $T_{c,\min}>0$. Only for $T_{c,\min}=0$ does it become a power law, $Δλ\propto T^n$ with $n\approx1.7$, but then the onset of screening drops to $T_p=T_{c,\max}/2$. Weighting the $T_{c}$ distribution towards $T_c\to0$ (more low-$T_{c}$ domains) can bring $n$ closer to 1 ($n\approx1.2$), but simultaneously pushes the apparent transition, $T_p$, more than an order of magnitude below $T_{c,\max}$. For d-wave domains, the linear term survives, and its relative slope is enhanced almost fourfold for $T_{c,\min}=0$.   Hence, a $T$-linear $λ(T)$ measured in a film with screening onset within a factor of a few of $T_{c,\max}$ by whole-sample or mutual-inductance part-sample measurements cannot originate from $T_c$ mosaicity in a fully gapped superconductor.
summary: This theoretical study investigates whether spatial variations in the critical temperature ($T_c$) within a superconducting film can account for an observed T-linear temperature dependence in the London penetration depth. By modeling the film as a random mosaic, the authors demonstrate that such a linear behavior is inconsistent with the physics of fully gapped superconductors unless the screening onset is significantly lower than the maximum local $T_c$. The work helps distinguish between intrinsic nodal behavior and disorder effects in superconducting films.
main_problem: To investigate whether the apparent T-linear temperature dependence of the London penetration depth, $\lambda(T)$, measured in superconducting films can be explained by spatial inhomogeneity in the local critical temperature ($T_c$).
main_result: The study concludes that a T-linear $\lambda(T)$ measured by whole-sample techniques cannot originate from $T_c$ mosaicity in a fully gapped superconductor if the screening onset is close to the maximum local $T_c$.
method: The authors modeled the film as a random Voronoi mosaic of superconducting domains and used London electrodynamics to calculate the macroscopic magnetic susceptibility and superfluid density.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting film modeled as a random Voronoi mosaic of domains, each possessing an independent local transition temperature ($T_c$) distributed between $T_{c,	ext{min}}$ and $T_{c,	ext{max}}$. The response is analyzed for both s-wave and d-wave pairing symmetries.
key_observables: London penetration depth $\lambda(T)$, superfluid density $ho_s(T)$, and the percolation temperature $T_p$.
important_parameters: The ratio of the screening onset temperature to $T_{c,	ext{max}}$, and the minimum local $T_c$ ($T_{c,	ext{min}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the thin-sheet limit, weak-coupling clean limit, and that the local London response is sufficient to describe the macroscopic behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mosaic realization, the continuous rise of the magnetic susceptibility derivative ($	ext{d}\chi/	ext{d}T$) below the percolation threshold, and the comparison between effective and area-averaged superfluid densities.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the discrepancy between local and global measurements. It then develops the $T_c$-mosaic model using Voronoi tessellation and London electrodynamics. Key results are presented by analyzing the temperature dependence of $\lambda(T)$ for s-wave and d-wave cases, leading to the final conclusion regarding the origin of T-linear behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for interpreting transport measurements in complex, disordered superconducting materials, which is highly relevant to understanding real-world superconducting devices.
